title: MacaulayWinter/seq-triage pipeline parameters
description: Detect sequencing platform, validate metadata, route QC, summarise

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Where the samplesheet comes from and where results go.

input.description: Samplesheet CSV: one row per sample, columns sample, fastq_1, fastq_2, platform, sample_type, molecule.
input.help_text: fastq_2, platform and sample_type are optional. Leave platform blank to have it detected from the reads.

outdir.description: Directory for results. Created if it does not exist.

metric_guide.description: TSV of metric definitions and warn/fail thresholds used by the summary report.
metric_guide.help_text: Defaults to assets/metric_guide.tsv. Supply your own to apply local thresholds without editing the pipeline.

publish_dir_mode.description: How results are written to outdir.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: copy is the default so that deleting work/ never empties results/.

contamination_screen.title: Contamination screen
contamination_screen.description: Optional: host and contaminant screening with Kraken2 (all routed samples) and Bracken (Illumina, species-level re-estimation).

kraken2_db.description: Kraken2 database: a directory containing hash.k2d, opts.k2d and taxo.k2d, or a .tar.gz of one. Leave unset to skip the screen; the report then says 'not screened'.
kraken2_db.help_text: Species-level results depend on the database. Validated results are reported per database in docs/validation.md.

kraken2_memory_mapping.description: Read the Kraken2 database from disk instead of loading it into memory. Slower, but fits a laptop.

bracken_read_length.description: Read length Bracken uses; the database must contain a matching database<N>mers.kmer_distrib file (prebuilt databases include 100, 150, 200, 250, 300).

species_groups.description: TSV of species judged as one group by the contamination screen (e.g. E. coli and Shigella), with the reason for each.

kraken2_batch.description: Classify every sample in one Kraken2 task, reading the database once (it stays in the node's file cache and each sample uses it with --memory-mapping).
kraken2_batch.help_text: Use with big databases (the full Standard database is ~94 GB), where loading it once per sample dominates the run. Samples then run one after another, and -resume reruns the whole batch if any sample changes. Results are identical to the default per-sample mode.
